Outlet: CNBC, published Fri Nov 6 2026 12:06 AM EST, updated Fri Nov 6 2026 2:54 PM EST. By Lee Ying Shan
Oil prices tumble for the week as investors weigh Iran conflict risk after midterm elections

Key Points: Rapidan Energy Group President Bob McNally told CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia" that he sees an "80% probability of military fighting resuming." Oil prices are down sharply since the start of the week amid fresh hopes for a diplomatic breakthrough to end the Mideast conflict.

Crude oil prices on Friday posted a steep weekly loss, as investors weighed the risk of renewed military escalation between the U.S. and Iran following the midterm elections.

International benchmark Brent crude futures added 3 cents to close at $98.32 per barrel. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures gained 31 cents to settle at $90.83 per barrel. Brent fell more than 16% for the week while U.S. crude lost nearly 13%.

Investors are assessing whether the conclusion of the U.S. midterm elections could pave the way for renewed actions against Iran, potentially threatening oil supplies from the Middle East.

Bob McNally, Rapidan Energy Group founder and president, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia" that he forecasts "both oil benchmarks could climb above $100 a barrel."

However, hopes for a diplomatic resolution have also emerged after Iran reportedly sent a nuclear proposal to Washington through Qatar, Reuters reported, citing a senior Iranian official.

Iran reported three additional attacks on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, while data from the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) indicated that attacks on vessels were continuing at a near-record rate.

McNally: "President Donald Trump is determined, as a legacy item, almost at all costs, to prevent Iran from getting a nuclear weapon." He added: "The Iranian regime, on the other hand, is not willing to do it. And as long as that core difference in that deal space is absent, the escalation dynamic remains in place."

McNally's view is shared by other analysts, including Lombard Odier's chief economist Samy Chaar and head of investment strategy Luca Bindelli.
